recommendations.title: Eliminate render-blocking resources
recommendations.description: Resources are blocking the first paint of your page. Consider delivering critical JS/CSS inline and deferring all non-critical JS/styles. Learn how to eliminate render-blocking resources.

recommendations.title: Properly size images
recommendations.description: Serve images that are appropriately-sized to save cellular data and improve load time. Learn how to size images.

recommendations.title: Reduce unused CSS
recommendations.description: Reduce unused rules from stylesheets and defer CSS not used for above-the-fold content to decrease bytes consumed by network activity. Learn how to reduce unused CSS.

recommendations.title: Reduce unused JavaScript
recommendations.description: Reduce unused JavaScript and defer loading scripts until they are required to decrease bytes consumed by network activity. Learn how to reduce unused JavaScript.

recommendations.title: Serve images in next-gen formats
recommendations.description: Image formats like WebP and AVIF often provide better compression than PNG or JPEG, which means faster downloads and less data consumption. Learn more about modern image formats.

recommendations.title: Reduce JavaScript execution time
recommendations.description: Consider reducing the time spent parsing, compiling, and executing JS. You may find delivering smaller JS payloads helps with this. Learn how to reduce Javascript execution time.

recommendations.title: Minimize main-thread work
recommendations.description: Consider reducing the time spent parsing, compiling and executing JS. You may find delivering smaller JS payloads helps with this. Learn how to minimize main-thread work

recommendations.title: Reduce the impact of third-party code
recommendations.description: Third-party code can significantly impact load performance. Limit the number of redundant third-party providers and try to load third-party code after your page has primarily finished loading. Learn how to minimize third-party impact.

aiSummaries.text:
Here is a summary of the latest website crawl results:

* **Key Finding:** The automated test stopped almost immediately, evaluating only two pages. This indicates the test was incomplete and did not scan the actual content of the website.
* **Primary Risk:** Because nearly the entire site was skipped, any broken links, visual bugs, or performance issues on your main pages remain undetected.
* **Required Action:** The technical team needs to check why the testing tool was blocked or restricted (e.g., due to security settings or configuration issues) and rerun the scan so we can get a complete picture of the site's health.

aiSummaries.text:
**Summary of Broken Link Scan Results:**

- **All scanned pages have broken links:** Both pages tested on the website contain broken links, indicating a widespread issue that affects the entire site.  
- **Key broken links:** The same two links are broken across both pages: a Facebook link (`https://www.facebook.com/contentbloomwcm/`) and an internal link (`https://contentbloom.com/xmlrpc.php`).  
- **Risks:** These broken links can harm user experience, SEO rankings, and brand credibility, as visitors may encounter errors when trying to access important resources.  
- **Action needed:** Prioritize fixing the two broken links, especially the internal link (`/xmlrpc.php`), as it may indicate a server or configuration issue. Additionally, verify the status of the Facebook page to ensure it’s active and correctly linked.

aiSummaries.text:
**Summary of Page Performance Scan Results:**

- **Mobile Performance is Critically Low:** The average mobile score is 30, indicating significant performance issues that could negatively impact user experience and SEO. The homepage and blog page are particularly slow on mobile, with load times exceeding 10 seconds for key metrics like Largest Contentful Paint (LCP).  
- **Desktop Performance is Strong:** The average desktop score is 83, showing that the site performs well for desktop users.  
- **Key Action Items:**  
  1. **Eliminate Render-Blocking Resources:** This is the most widespread issue, affecting all pages, and addressing it could save up to 1.37 seconds on mobile.  
  2. **Optimize Images:** Properly sizing and deferring offscreen images (especially on mobile) could significantly reduce load times and data usage.  
  3. **Reduce Unused CSS and Minify CSS:** These changes would streamline page loading and improve efficiency across both mobile and desktop.  
- **High-Risk Pages:** The blog page and homepage on mobile require immediate attention due to extremely slow load times and poor performance scores.  

**Action Needed:** Prioritize mobile optimizations, focusing on render-blocking resources and image handling, to improve user experience and search rankings.
